tenantNotes: graph-core itself is tenant-agnostic: Graph and the constraint/schema functions all take an already-resolved `Client` (or are pure TS). Multi-tenant DB selection lives in db.ts via `getDb(namespace)`, which maps each namespace to its own `file:${namespace}.db` libSQL database (DB-per-tenant), optionally addressed off `SQLD_URL` as an embedded replica. So isolation is one physical SQLite/libSQL DB per namespace. For Postgres the natural port is schema-per-tenant (or database-per-tenant): `getDb(namespace)` would hand back a pool scoped to a Postgres schema (SET search_path) or a separate database, but none of the four reviewed files would change — they consume whatever Client/pool they're given.

n/a within these files. There is no namespace/multi-tenant DB selection in temporal-retrieval; every function takes a single `raw: Client` handle and operates on one database. Tenant/namespace isolation (if any) is decided by the caller that constructs the Client (e.g. per-tenant libSQL DB file/URL). Porting to Postgres would surface a tenant decision (schema-per-tenant search_path, a tenant_id column + RLS, or database-per-tenant), but nothing here encodes it today — the stable API passes a connection in, so the tenant model stays the caller's concern.

n/a — none of these modules implement namespace/tenant selection. Every function takes a libSQL `Client` (the `raw` param) supplied by the caller; tenant/database routing is entirely the caller's responsibility. There is no schema-qualification of table names (tables like `nodes`, `edge_versions`, `node_analytics`, `nodes_fts` are unqualified), so a Postgres schema-per-tenant or search_path strategy would have to be introduced at the connection/client layer outside this area, or table names would need qualification threaded through the SQL builders.

DB-per-project (the strongest isolation tier). The control-plane registry (a single shared libSQL DB) maps projectId -> projects.db_namespace (UNIQUE), e.g. acme__alpha. authorize() returns ONLY that dbNamespace string (never a sqld token, §2.9). getDb(namespace) turns the string into a concrete data DB: url=file:<namespace>.db locally, and in replica mode appends it to SQLD_URL (`${SQLD_URL}/${namespace}`) as a distinct sqld namespace/database, opening a libSQL embedded replica that pulls from the primary every syncInterval (default 60s). Only the server holds SQLD_TOKEN; end users get no DB credential. One cached Client per namespace (Map in db.ts) — explicitly NOT a global singleton, which would collapse tenants. serve.ts adds a confused-deputy guard (URL :tenant must equal principal.tenantId) and a per-namespace one-time init guard (WeakMap keyed by Client) in authz.ts. Postgres equivalent: DB-per-tenant (separate database/conn string per namespace — closest, but cross-DB DDL/migrations are heavier and connection-count grows), schema-per-tenant (single DB, SET search_path TO <namespace> per checkout — best fit for the namespace->one-string mapping and shared-server-credential model), or row-level (shared tables + tenant_id + RLS — weakest isolation, cheapest). The embedded-replica/syncUrl/syncInterval/.sync() and sync-before-serve readiness mechanics have no PG analog and would be replaced by PG read replicas + connectivity/replication-lag readiness checks.

Database-per-namespace. The auth package contains zero tenant/namespace columns or predicates; isolation comes entirely from operating on a Graph whose `g.raw` is a libSQL Client bound to a single per-project database file (core's getDb(namespace) -> `file:${namespace}.db`, optionally a synced replica). The HTTP layer (http.ts) makes the operator responsible: AuthServeConfig.resolveAuth maps the request (tenant/project route params) to a `${project}__auth` namespace and returns the Auth engine bound to that DB. Porting to Postgres requires deciding between keeping DB/schema-per-namespace (resolution stays in core) vs. introducing a tenant_id column + RLS (would require touching every SQL predicate in store.ts/check.ts/list.ts).

The admin backend does not implement tenant isolation itself; it relies on core. It seeds a control plane (createTenant/createProject/createUser/addMembership) where each project carries a db_namespace string. Two auth realms: tenant-scoped routes use an authenticate() that mints an operator Principal { userId:"operator", tenantId: route :tenant param, operator:true } from the dev bearer token (operator bypasses membership checks); /admin/* uses adminAuthenticate() validating the same token. Namespace-to-connection resolution (db_namespace -> file:<namespace>.db, cached per namespace, lazy init) happens entirely in core (packages/core/src/db.ts getDb and authz.ts resolveProjectDb), not in the admin backend. The admin backend's only namespace-aware code is the SQLite-file teardown for DEMO_NS=\"dev_admin\".

Two layers. (1) Connection/namespace selection is via `getDb(namespace, cfg)` — the namespace string (control-plane `db_namespace`, e.g. `acme__alpha`) maps 1:1 to a physical libSQL DB: a `file:${namespace}.db` locally, or addressed off `SQLD_URL` (`${base}/${namespace}`) in embedded-replica mode. One cached Client per namespace; NEVER a global singleton (isolation guarantee §2.9). (2) HTTP consumers select tenant/project through URL path params `/t/:tenant/p/:project/...`; the serve middleware runs `authenticate` → Principal { userId, tenantId, operator? }, then `resolveProjectDb`/`graphForProject(control, principal, projectId, op)` → authorize (project ∈ tenant, role ≥ op) → `getDb(dbNamespace)` → a per-project `Graph`. End users never receive a DB credential; the server is the only sqld credential holder. Auth package mirrors this: the operator-supplied `resolveAuth(c, principal, op)` callback owns tenant/project → `${project}__auth` namespace resolution. For Postgres, namespace→physical-DB must become namespace→schema (search_path) or a tenant-id key over a shared pool; this is the single biggest tenant-model porting decision, and it is reachable entirely through getDb/resolveProjectDb without changing the public path-param contract or Principal shape.

File-per-tenant on SQLite: db.ts getDb(namespace) caches one @libsql/client per namespace pointed at `file:${namespace}.db` (or an embedded-replica URL under SQLD_URL). Control-plane (tenants/users/memberships, control-plane.ts) lives in a SEPARATE DB from project namespace DBs; in tests it is a separate `:memory:` client. Teardown evicts the cached client (c.close()) and rmSync's the `<ns>.db`/`-wal`/`-shm` files (the leaked ns_*.db files in repo root come from this). Postgres equivalent: schema-per-tenant (CREATE SCHEMA / SET search_path) or database-per-tenant on one server, with a connection pool keyed by namespace; DROP SCHEMA CASCADE for teardown; .sync()/embedded-replica has no analog.
risksByArea: graph-core

The public Graph method signatures and types (define-graph-schema.ts especially) must stay byte-stable — they're the SDK surface. define-graph-schema.ts is pure TS and ports unchanged, but graph.ts couples those stable types to libSQL-specific InStatement/InValue/Row/Client/Transaction imports; swapping the driver means re-typing internals without altering the public shapes.

`graph.raw: Client` is documented as PUBLIC and read directly by P4/P6/P7 (retrieval, embeddings, etc.). Changing the client type from `@libsql/client` to a pg pool is a breaking change that ripples far beyond these four files.

The FTS5 external-content + content_rowid='ver' + sync-trigger design is the hardest port: it's wired to the INTEGER PRIMARY KEY rowid and the exported NODES_FTS_TRIGGER_DDL const, which P13's bulk loader DROPs/recreates around imports. Moving to a tsvector column changes that DROP/recreate contract and the as-of-lexical search join in nodeFilter.

NV_EMB_IDX_DDL is exported and DROPped/recreated by the P13 bulk loader (deferred index build). Its DDL is libsql_vector_idx-specific; the pgvector HNSW/ivfflat replacement has very different build cost/semantics, so the deferral story must be re-validated.

The conditional-close + SQLITE_BUSY retry envelope (runWriteBatch/runConditionalClose) encodes SQLite's single-writer lock model and busy_timeout=0-on-interactive-tx quirk. Under Postgres MVCC the failure modes differ (40001/40P01 serialization/deadlock); naive translation could either over-retry or miss real serialization failures, risking interval overlap in the temporal model.

The B5 emb NULL/vector('[]') two-branch logic exists solely to dodge a libSQL dim-0 throw. If ported carelessly to pgvector (which doesn't throw), the dead branch could mask a real binding bug; needs deliberate simplification, not mechanical translation.

`props` is currently TEXT with JS-side JSON.stringify/JSON.parse. Switching to jsonb changes what the `pg` driver returns (auto-parsed objects) — if not handled, rowToNode/updateNode would double-parse or receive objects where strings are expected, silently corrupting props round-trips.

Identifier inlining via safeIdent/sqlLiteral in constraints.ts must be preserved (Postgres also can't bind identifiers in DDL); the `ux_${kind.length}_${kind}_${prop}` index-name disambiguation logic is subtle and must survive the port intact or uniqueness silently goes unenforced.

init() uses libSQL-only `executeMultiple` (no `;`-splitting) for the whole DDL script; Postgres drivers have no equivalent, so the init path needs restructuring and the IF NOT EXISTS idempotency (esp. CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS, unsupported in PG) must be reworked to CREATE OR REPLACE without breaking re-run safety.
temporal-retrieval

asOfPredicate(alias) returns a raw SQL string fragment with positional `?` binds baked in (`alias.valid_from <= ? AND ? < alias.valid_to`). It is a PUBLIC export reused by other query builders; changing to $n placeholders for Postgres breaks every caller that composes it and assumes two positional binds. The placeholder convention is part of its de-facto contract.

The ANN seed correctness depends on libSQL's vector_top_k returning rows in distance order and on MIN(v.id) being a valid rank proxy. In pgvector you order by real distance; behavior (and result ordering, hence RRF fusion output) will differ subtly, which could change retrieved subgraphs and break golden tests even though the public API is unchanged.

RRF in hybrid.ts fuses on logical id but seed RANK comes from SQL ORDER BY (FTS rank, ANN rowid). Postgres FTS ts_rank vs FTS5 bm25, and pgvector distance vs vector_top_k order, will produce different rank positions -> different fused seed sets. The stable-API guarantee covers shape, not exact result ordering; downstream tests asserting specific ids/order are at risk.

The recursive-walk cycle guard encodes ids in a comma-delimited string and matches with LIKE '%,'||id||',%'. If any id can contain a comma (ULIDs cannot, but the type is `string`), the guard is unsafe. A Postgres array-based guard removes this latent coupling but is a behavioral rewrite of the hot path.

Bare-column GROUP BY (SELECT body, uri, MIN(depth) ... GROUP BY id) is invalid in Postgres and silently relies on SQLite picking the row at MIN(depth). The DISTINCT ON rewrite must replicate the exact 'row at minimum depth' tie-break or retrieved body/uri could change.

FTS5 external-content + AFTER INSERT trigger + 'rebuild'/DROP-during-bulk-load is an architecture the bulk loader (P13) and schema.ts both depend on via the exported NODES_FTS_TRIGGER_DDL constant. Moving to a generated tsvector column removes the trigger entirely, so the exported DDL constants (NV_EMB_IDX_DDL, NODES_FTS_TRIGGER_DDL) — which are PUBLIC and consumed by the loader's drop/recreate logic — change meaning and may break that loader.

Pervasive positional `?` binding with hand-counted per-CTE-side arg duplication (t pushed 2x/4x; rels pushed per side) is fragile to port to $n; an off-by-one in the manual arg arrays would mis-bind temporal predicates and silently return wrong as-of results rather than erroring.

upcast.ts is pure TS with zero SQL — no porting risk itself, but it JSON.parses stored props TEXT. If Postgres stores props as jsonb (not text), the read path returns an object not a string; storedVersion/_v handling and the stamp() write path assume a plain object already, so keeping props as `text` (not jsonb) avoids a type-shift, but that forgoes Postgres JSON indexing.

loadEmbeddings + MMR cosine run client-side in JS via vector_extract+JSON.parse. In Postgres pgvector you could push cosine into SQL (1-(emb<=>q)); keeping it client-side is portable but wastes the typed vector. The JSON.parse(String(row.e)) line hard-assumes the libSQL vector_extract text shape and must change for pgvector's `[..]` text serialization.
query-graph

CompiledPattern.sql/args is a documented, test-asserted public contract (acceptance §16: '?' count === args.length, exact param order). Porting to $n placeholders changes the SQL string AND arg-ordering expectations — any test or consumer that inspects .toSQL() output will break. This is the tightest stable-API constraint in the area.

The sql-mode shortestPath relies on ORDER BY inside a recursive CTE (a SQLite-only priority-queue behavior). Postgres forbids this; a naive port silently loses best-first pruning and can enumerate exponentially many paths or change results. Highest-risk semantic divergence.
journey.ts uses scalar MAX(a,b); in Postgres MAX is an aggregate. A mechanical port will either error or aggregate incorrectly — must become GREATEST. Easy to miss.

TEXT-path cycle guards (path LIKE '%,'||x||',%') can false-positive when one id is a substring of another; comma delimiters mitigate but ULID safety depends on the delimiter. An array-based port changes behavior subtly and must preserve depth/hops/path semantics that downstream tests assert.

FOREVER sentinel (8640000000000000) is interpolated as a bare literal in many predicates and is the linchpin of the half-open temporal model; if the porting switches to NULL valid_to, EVERY predicate here (and snapshotCSR's t>=FOREVER routing) must change consistently or temporal correctness breaks.

Vector (libsql_vector_idx / vector()) and FTS5 (external-content + 'rebuild') are design-decision swaps to pgvector/tsvector. The drop-index/drop-trigger-around-bulk choreography in bulkLoad is tied to those exact DDL constants (NV_EMB_IDX_DDL, NODES_FTS_TRIGGER_DDL from schema.ts); changing the index types ripples into bulk.ts even though bulk.ts only references the DDL by import.

raw.batch(stmts,'write') (libSQL atomic batch) is used in both persist() and bulkLoad(); there is no node-postgres equivalent. A client abstraction is needed, and the bulkLoad comment documents a libSQL :memory: transaction() quirk that does NOT apply to pg — porting must not blindly preserve the 'use batch not transaction' choice.
chunkSize defaults (100) and the CHUNK=500 in persist are tuned to SQLite bound-parameter limits; Postgres limits differ (65535 params), so values may be suboptimal but not incorrect.

Interpolated identifiers (${metric}, ${col}, ${v.min/max}, ${maxFanout}, ${FOREVER}) are guarded by whitelists/int-validation, not parameterized. Any port must preserve those guards (Object.hasOwn check in topNodes is explicitly an injection defense).
platform

Connection-count blowup: the per-namespace Client cache (db.ts Map) is sound for cheap embedded SQLite files but a naive 1:1 namespace->PG-pool map exhausts Postgres connections; needs a bounded shared pool or pgbouncer, changing evict/closeAll to async pool.end(). This is the single biggest porting risk to the isolation model.

getDb is synchronous and returns a Client immediately; a PG port that needs to CREATE DATABASE / set search_path / await a pool makes resolution async, rippling into resolveProjectDb/graphForProject signatures (those are already async, but getDb being sync is relied upon).

DbConfig/getDb are part of the stable public API; changing the signature (sync->async, adding pool config) or the meaning of namespace (file vs schema vs row filter) breaks consumers and the stable-API guarantee.
Two independent SQLITE_CONSTRAINT string checks (admin.ts:47, serve.ts:236) must both be migrated to PG SQLSTATE class 23 codes; missing one silently turns 400s into 500s.

Per-tenant lazy init (authz.ts initOnce) runs schema.ts DDL containing SQLite-only vector index (libsql_vector_idx) + FTS5 virtual table + PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL on first touch; the platform files invoke this but the heavy dialect work is in schema.ts (separate area) — porting platform alone is insufficient without the schema port, hidden coupling via init().

applyConnPragmas (foreign_keys/busy_timeout) is invoked from control-plane initControl and assumed elsewhere per-connection; dropping it for PG is correct but any code relying on FK enforcement only after the pragma must be re-verified (PG always enforces, so behavior strengthens, not weakens).
syncIfReplica + Readiness latch are wired into serve.ts /ready gating; removing embedded-replica sync means markReady() must be re-driven by a different signal or /ready stays permanently gated.

governance.ts inlines maxRows/maxFanout into SQL strings via floored integers; safe and portable, but it couples to recursive-CTE SQL whose CTE names (adj/walk/adj_deg) and structure live in other modules — verify those compile under PG WITH RECURSIVE before trusting fanoutJoin/applyLimit unchanged.
Operator authz bypass (authz.ts operator flag) still relies on the project-tenant guard running first; any reordering during a port could open a cross-tenant leak for operator principals.
auth-pkg

check.ts and expand.ts do NOT use SQL recursion — relation expansion is recursive in TypeScript, issuing one edgesInto() query per node/relation step (N+1). Postgres round-trip latency is higher than an in-process SQLite file, so the same code will be markedly slower; may need batching or a SQL-side recursive CTE rewrite to stay performant, which is a behavioral/perf change not covered by the stable API.

Idempotency of writeTuple/ensureObject and atomicity of deleteTuple currently lean on SQLite's single-writer serialization (explicitly noted in comments). Postgres allows concurrent writers, so the NOT-EXISTS guards can race and produce duplicate live tuples or double-revokes unless replaced with real UNIQUE constraints/ON CONFLICT and explicit transactions. This is a correctness risk, not just syntax.

FOREVER = 8640000000000000 must map to BIGINT in Postgres (overflows INT4); node-postgres returns BIGINT as string, so the existing Number(vf) cast pattern must be applied consistently or comparisons silently break.

json_extract(props,'$.subjectRelation') vs Postgres jsonb `->>'...'` has subtly different NULL semantics (missing key vs SQL NULL); the IS NULL branch used to distinguish direct vs userset tuples must be re-validated to avoid mis-classifying tuples.

The package depends on core's `nodes`/`edges` live VIEWs and node_versions/edge_versions/identity tables. Any Postgres port of core's schema must preserve these view names and the valid_to=FOREVER live semantics, or every query here breaks — tight coupling to core schema across a package boundary.

listObjects relies on UNION (dedup) in the recursive CTE for cycle termination and on ORDER BY/LIMIT being in the outer query only; Postgres recursive-CTE restrictions (no aggregate/ORDER BY/LIMIT inside the recursive term, stricter column typing) must be checked, and the SCAN_CAP/keyset cursor contract (nextCursor can be non-null with empty objects) must remain identical to not break paging clients.

Stable wire/JSON contract of http.ts (route paths, request/response shapes, error-status mapping including the 'auth:' message-prefix -> 400 heuristic) must be preserved verbatim through any DB port; error messages thrown from store/model are part of observable behavior.
admin-backend
The SQLite-file teardown (rmSync of .db/-wal/-shm) silently no-ops on Postgres; without replacing it with a schema/database reset, the dev demo would accumulate stale state instead of starting fresh.

control plane uses url ":memory:" — there is no Postgres equivalent, so the dev harness must adopt an external/throwaway Postgres instance, changing startup ergonomics (was zero-dependency in-process).

The real porting work is hidden in core (db.ts getDb, authz.ts resolveProjectDb, control-plane.ts DDL/SQL); this admin-backend area looks deceptively small but is fully coupled to core's namespace=file model via the db_namespace it seeds.

DEMO_NS string "dev_admin" is already a valid Postgres identifier, but any future namespaces must satisfy Postgres identifier rules (lowercasing, length, no leading digit) if mapped to schema/db names.

The UI (packages/admin/src/lib/api.ts) is tightly bound to the exact route shapes, the {error} envelope, the 401 contract, and the dbNamespace field; the Postgres port must preserve all of these or the SPA breaks even though it never touches the DB directly.
public-api

Pervasive Client leak: `@libsql/client`'s `Client` type appears in the SIGNATURE of nearly every public entrypoint (Graph constructor + public `raw` field, ServeConfig.control, AdminConfig.control, all control-plane fns, authz authorize/resolveProjectDb, init/ensureColumn, retrieve). Introducing an abstract DbClient interface is the keystone refactor; if the libSQL Client does not structurally satisfy the new interface, every libSQL caller breaks — must design the interface as a strict subset of what libSQL Client already provides.

`Graph.raw` is documented as PUBLIC and consumed directly by retrieve/history/journey (and auth via g.raw). Any consumer code in the wild may call libSQL-specific methods on `.raw` (e.g. `.sync()`, `.batch()`, libSQL transaction semantics) — narrowing its type to a portable interface can silently break those call sites even though it compiles for first-party code.

DbConfig is a user-constructed object whose three fields (authToken/syncUrl/syncInterval) are meaningless in Postgres. Removing or repurposing them is a breaking change; they must be kept optional/deprecated to preserve compile-compat, risking confusing config where libSQL fields silently no-op on Postgres.

Exported DDL constants (CONTROL_SCHEMA, NODES_FTS_TRIGGER_DDL, NV_EMB_IDX_DDL, `schema`) are raw SQLite/libSQL dialect strings in the public API. If consumers run them directly they are unportable; they need per-dialect variants or deprecation, but changing/removing them is API-breaking.

Placeholder convention: all internal SQL uses `?` (positional). Postgres requires `$1..$n`. This is internal, but it rides on the same publicly-typed clients — the driver abstraction MUST own placeholder rewriting or every query breaks on Postgres.

Vector + FTS features (retrieve, hybridRetrieve, NV_EMB_IDX_DDL, FTS5 triggers) are libSQL-native; the Postgres path needs pgvector + tsvector. RetrieveOpts/HybridRetrieveOpts/RetrievedNode are public types — their shapes must stay stable even though the underlying engine differs (e.g. distance metric semantics may subtly change scores, a behavioral-compat risk).

Tenant model coupling: getDb hardcodes one-DB-per-namespace (`file:` / sqld URL). The §2.9 isolation guarantee is currently 'by construction' (separate physical DB per project). Moving to Postgres schemas or tenant-id rows weakens that to logical isolation — a security-posture change hidden behind a stable public surface; consumers relying on physical isolation could be surprised.
`AppType` is already a known-limited export (env-level only due to isolatedDeclarations). Touching serve.ts during the port must not further degrade the typed-client story documented in serve.ts.
build-test

No driver abstraction exists: every src module and every test imports `@libsql/client` `Client` directly and emits raw SQLite SQL. Adding PG is not a config change — it requires either a real dialect/adapter layer or a parallel implementation, touching ~all of core/src.

Test harness is the hardest coupling: ~30 test files call createClient({url:':memory:'}) or file: DBs with libSQL-specific teardown. There is no shared makeTestDb() factory to swap, so PG support means refactoring every test or introducing a harness shim first.

Vector (F32_BLOB/vector_top_k) and FTS5 cannot be tested on pg-mem — they need a real Postgres with pgvector + tsvector. testcontainers is the realistic path but adds Docker dependency and breaks the windows-latest CI matrix leg.

Several tests rely on libSQL-specific quirks (`:memory:` connection detaches on transaction rollback, table_info hides generated columns so table_xinfo is used, WAL/SHM sidecar files). These workarounds are wrong/absent under PG and their removal must not silently change behavior the tests assert.

Positional `?` placeholders and libSQL verbs (executeMultiple/batch('write')/transaction('write')/sync) are everywhere; a naive port risks SQL-injection regressions or param-renumbering bugs ($1 vs ?).
STORED-only generated columns in PG (no VIRTUAL) and the rowid->ver->FTS content_rowid coupling mean schema.ts/constraints.ts changes can break the vector_top_k/FTS row mapping in non-obvious ways.
build/exports: single `.` export and unconditional @libsql/client dependency — shipping PG support without conditional exports + optional peer deps would force every consumer to install both drivers.
Leaked repo-root ns_*.db artifacts indicate tests already write to cwd, not just tmpdir — a PG harness must ensure no equivalent cross-test schema leakage.
